subject: Polaris Health — Committed GPU pool & isolation: post-call recap and next steps
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lisa Parker <lisa.parker@polarishealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-28T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Polaris Health — Committed GPU pool & isolation: post-call recap and next steps

Hi Lisa — thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so everyone has the same picture and a short list of immediate next steps.

High-level needs you confirmed:
- Production inference for clinical NLP pipelines with strict data residency and isolation requirements (PH patient data).
- Predictable tail latency for inference at 99th percentile (goal: p99 <= 300ms on 512-token requests).
- Regular throughput bursts tied to nightly batch scoring (up to ~3k concurrent requests) plus steady daytime traffic (~200 qps).
- Compliance: SOC2 evidence, audit logs retention (12 months), KMS integration.

What we proposed during the call:
1) Committed GPU pool (reserved capacity) — isolated tenant pool with dedicated GPUs (silo) to guarantee throughput and avoid noisy-neighbor variance.
2) VPC-only private deployment for data isolation with optional peering or PrivateLink to your environment.
3) Autoscale policy: policy-based buffer with burst-to-shared fallback for extreme events; can be locked to prevent cross-tenant spillover.
4) SLA targets: 99.9% availability for the dedicated pool; p95 latency SLOs in contract, and proposal to surface p99 tail targets in the tech appendix.

Actionable next steps (owner in parentheses):
- Redwood to send a draft SLA and a high-level network diagram (Jasmine) — attached: sla-draft-v1.pdf, network-arch.png.
- Polaris to confirm peak nightly window and provide estimated concurrent requests during peak (Lisa).
- Redwood Solutions (Rishi) to map GPU sizing options (A100 80GB vs H100 80GB) and expected qps per model; will attach a short MOP spreadsheet (polaris-mop.xlsx).
- Schedule 30-min procurement handoff including your contracts team (Evan) to review pricing & T&Cs (both).

Risks / open questions we captured:
- Do you require physical on-prem (air-gapped) deployment for any of the workloads, or is VPC-only acceptable?
- Key rotation and HSM: who will own KMS (Polaris-managed vs Redwood-managed)?
- If behavioral data retention needs exceed 12 months, we should note that in the proposal.

Attached: polaris-mop.xlsx (workload sizing stub), sla-draft-v1.pdf (initial SLA items), network-arch.png (VPC peering options).

I pushed proposed times for the procurement call — available Mon/Tue next week 10–12 PT. Which works best?

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0191
Redwood Inference — production-grade LLM inference

From: Lisa Parker <lisa.parker@polarishealth.com>

Date: 2027-04-28T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Polaris Health — Committed GPU pool & isolation: post-call recap and next steps

Jasmine — thanks for the clear recap, this aligns with our notes. A couple of quick items from our side: 

- Peak nightly window is 02:00–04:30 local time (central), roughly 2,800 concurrent inferences at the current model size. Daytime burst pattern can spike to ~500 qps for short 10–15 minute events.
- VPC-only is preferred; we may consider on-prem for a narrow subset of models later but that would be a separate procurement track.
- Polaris will own KMS initially; we'll need Redwood to support our KMS (Azure Key Vault) integration with HSM-backed keys.

Evan — looping you in to coordinate contract timing & any required security addenda.

Can you confirm the estimated lead time from contract signing to a provisioned committed pool (we're aiming for early June if possible)? Also confirm whether the burst-to-shared fallback is opt-in — we prefer an opt-out model (i.e., stick to silo unless we explicitly enable sharing during an emergency).

Best,
Lisa
Lisa Parker
Head of ML Platforms, Polaris Health

Subject: Re: Polaris Health — Committed GPU pool & isolation: post-call recap and next steps

Lisa / Jasmine — quick technical notes and sizing guidance based on the numbers Lisa provided. Attaching the MOP with scenarios.

Sizing outline (ballpark):
- Option A (A100 80GB, FP16): 6 GPUs for steady-state + 4 GPUs buffer for nightly peak = 10 GPUs committed. Expected steady qps ~200, peak concurrency handling via batching ~2,800 requests in the 02:00–04:30 window.
- Option B (H100 80GB, TF32 / AMP): 4 GPUs steady + 4 buffer = 8 GPUs committed; better p99 tail but higher unit cost.

Performance notes:
- We recommend enabling KV-prefix caching for repeated patient lookups to keep p99 latency below 300ms for typical 512-token requests.
- Autoscale policy can be configured with strict capacity caps; the "burst-to-shared" behavior is an opt-in toggle in Redwood Console — default for Dedicated is to honor silo only. We can flip to opt-out for Polaris if you want the conservative default to be silo-only.

Security / compliance:
- We support Azure Key Vault integration and can pass HSM-backed keys through our private control plane.
- Audit logs: full request/response metadata (redacted PHI by default unless requested) can be retained for 12 months; we can extend on request with an add-on.

Next technical deliverables (this week):
- Updated MOP with per-model qps and recommended GPU profile (Rishi) — attached: polaris-mop.xlsx.
- Short appendix describing network peering options and firewall rules (Ben).

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to the MOP and the draft SOW.
